Hold the kind and span claims of the install-page pin (#289)

Make the self-checks of tools/test-install-page.py hold what its
docstrings say about the reader pin of check 7, and word those
docstrings so that they claim no more than the checks hold. The gate,
tools/check-install-page.py, is byte identical, so GATE_SHA256 and
READER_SHA256 are unchanged.

- Capture tuple, list and dict when the test is imported, as
  PLAIN_CONTAINERS beside PLAIN_TYPES, and compare the exact type of a
  value with them by identity in plain_data(). Each kind, plain data
  included, is then compared by identity with a type that the test
  captured when it was imported (PLAIN_TYPES, PLAIN_CONTAINERS,
  PIN_KINDS).
- Add capture_problems(): with re.Pattern, types.ModuleType, the
  test's REPO_ROOT, tuple, list or dict rebound to a stand-in, 1 name
  at a time, pin_value() must still write a real value of that kind as
  before and refuse an instance of the stand-in. The exact type of a
  value is read with the builtin type(), which a rebinding of a builtin
  can change, a class that the reader pin does not see (residual 2); no
  check holds the capture of type.
- Derive refusal cases from the 3 capture tuples: for each of their 13
  kinds, an object whose class gives the kind as its __class__, and,
  for the 10 kinds that Python lets a class subclass, an instance of a
  bare subclass, so that each kind test of pin_value() and plain_data()
  must match the exact type. The 19 committed refused values are kept.
- Run the 2 replacements of REQUESTED_FILES on 3 base gates: the
  committed gate, one in which its statement shares its line with
  LOADED_SEGMENTS and REDIRECT_TARGETS and a comment, and one in which
  it spans 3 lines, each built gate first passing the reader pin.
- Rewrite the fixture PIN_SUBCLASS as 1 simple statement with the same
  meaning, a deliberate change of its contract: a class statement
  cannot follow a semicolon, so the committed form does not parse on
  the shared-line gate.
- Add to pin_value()'s docstring that it writes a module, a class or a
  path by its name, so a helper that one of them carries is in no
  digest here, and mark its refused values as examples. The pin holds
  the values that a reviewed gate defines in ordinary code, and
  scope_sentence_problems() fails each docstring of the file that says
  so without the words "a module, a class or a path by its name".
- Leave .github/squash/269.txt unchanged: it is the merged record of
  pull request 269, and whether merged records are amended is the
  maintainer's decision.
